prompt: Design a project management dashboard for software teams — track tasks across sprints, see team velocity metrics, organize work by priority and status, and drill into individual tasks for details and comments. Make it clean, fast, and professional.
title: Sprintboard

issues.description: The V17 gate reports the home screen is missing its primary action, despite the copy plan requiring a clear New task action. The active sprint dashboard therefore lacks the main affordance for creating work.

The V17 gate reports the detail screen is missing its primary action, despite the detail contract requiring Change status. A focused task view without a visible status-change affordance does not support the required workflow.

The V17 gate measures only one rendered list row, below the required minimum of four, even though the screen is required to show a populated sprint task table for operations. This makes task flow, blocked work, sorting, and inline updates effectively unavailable.

The V17 gate measures approximately 60% empty viewport and only about 40% content fill on the dashboard, while this product requires an information-dense active sprint workspace. The implemented render does not provide enough visible supporting context around the scoreboard, chart, and task table.

The V17 gate measures only two modules, approximately 20% content fill, and missing supporting context on the detail screen. The required single-task workflow must include facts, description, activity history, comments, and updates; the verified render is substantially too sparse for that contract.

Measured geometry reports the detail sections using the secondary and background surfaces are flush with rhythm=0 and flush=1. The detail pane and CTA band need at least the prescribed 32px section separation and alternating rhythm.

The deterministic V17 gate reports three modules instead of the dashboard minimum of four and no visible custom product-specific component. Add a supporting sprint insight or activity module without turning the page into a generic card grid.

The deterministic V17 gate reports two modules instead of the dashboard minimum of four and no visible custom product-specific component. The detail view needs richer, visibly structured task facts, activity, and comments while remaining a single-item workflow rather than a card stack.

TaskActivityRow, TaskFactRow, and TaskComment call Avatar with src, alt, and size="sm", but src/components/Avatar.jsx ignores src and initials, and expects size to be numeric. This can produce invalid sizing and blank initials in the detail activity and comment rows.

The screenshot contains a very large empty vertical region between the top workspace navigation and the detail hero, roughly 900px tall. This is not intentional breathing room; it pushes the focused task workflow far below the first viewport and violates the blocking large-gap rule.

The active sprint content begins after a very large empty vertical region below the workspace navigation, roughly 900px tall. The sprint scoreboard should be the dominant first-view moment, but the blank space overwhelms the screen.

The detail view presents Change Status in the hero and a second prominent Mark Complete action in Quick Actions. The brief requires one clear primary status action; these competing controls make the workflow ambiguous.

Task Details, Activity History, Comments, and Quick Actions read as multiple generic bordered cards stacked on a white canvas. The detail screen lacks the calm Notion-style alternation of a dominant tonal hero, plain content blocks, and divided rows; outline-only separation is a blocking visual defect.

The Description text is generic instructional copy — “Review the task’s workflow facts, description, updates, and comments...” — rather than a real description of the selected software task “Team offsite.” This makes the detail record feel like a template instead of a focused task.

The task facts visibly include assignee, sprint, story points, due date, and component, while status and priority only appear in the hero metadata. The requested focused workflow facts should be consolidated into an explicit, scannable fact set so status is not dependent on the hero badge.

The sprint scoreboard shows completion, active count, and blocked count, but no explicit Remaining points metric. “5/42 points” is embedded in supporting copy and does not satisfy the requested above-the-table remaining-points summary.
The compact status breakdown is incomplete: only Active and Blocked are shown. The sprint overview should visibly account for the full workflow status set, including completed and to-do work.

Velocity history shows a six-point line but only labels Sprint 1, Sprint 3, and Sprint 6 on the x-axis, and it does not show the current sprint target. The brief calls for the last six sprints beside the current target with readable labeling.

The scoreboard, velocity chart, recent activity, and table are all presented as lightly outlined white cards on a white canvas. This reads as assembled dashboard scaffolding rather than the Notion design language; use a dominant tonal scoreboard band, a distinct chart treatment, and divided task rows.

New task is present, but it is isolated in the workspace header rather than visually integrated with the search and status filter toolbar. The requested focused work controls should read as one toolbar containing search, one select filter, and the primary New task action.

reviewResult.summary: The screens compile and use an appropriate sidebar/topbar app shell with relevant software-team task data, but both verified renders fail the core two-screen UX contract. The home dashboard is too empty and does not visibly provide its New task action or a sufficiently populated task table. The detail view is substantially underfilled, lacks Change status and supporting activity/comment context, and has an Avatar prop mismatch that can break rendered task history. Detail spacing also violates the measured section rhythm.
requiredFixes: In src/screens/home.jsx, render the planned New task primary action prominently in the sprint toolbar or scoreboard and ensure the task table visibly contains at least four divided task rows with all required columns.
In src/screens/detail.jsx, render the Change status primary action as an obvious, functional control in the detail pane or CTA band.
In src/screens/detail.jsx, add the missing supporting task context: complete workflow facts, activity history, and comments/update UI for the single Design audit task.
In src/screens/home.jsx, reduce the measured empty viewport and increase dashboard content density while preserving the scoreboard, velocity chart, toolbar, and task rows.
In src/screens/detail.jsx, separate the secondary-background detail area from the background CTA band with the required rhythm spacing; the measured sections currently render flush.

In src/screens/detail.jsx and src/components/Avatar.jsx, align the Avatar API: detail passes src, alt, and size="sm", while Avatar only supports name, initials, numeric size, and ignores src. Use the supported props or update Avatar so avatars render with valid dimensions and accessible names.
detail: remove the approximately 900px empty vertical region between the workspace header and task content; bring the detail hero into the first viewport using the required 32–64px section rhythm.
home: remove the approximately 900px empty vertical region between the workspace header and sprint content; bring the sprint scoreboard into the first viewport.
detail: consolidate Change Status and Mark Complete into one clear primary status action; make Edit and other actions quiet secondary controls.
detail: replace the generic description with a specific description for the selected software task, and surface an explicit status fact alongside priority, assignee, sprint, points, and due date.
detail: redesign the task facts, activity, and comments as calm divided rows or tonal sections rather than a stack of lightly outlined cards.
home: add an explicit Remaining points metric and a complete compact status breakdown including at least To do, In progress, Completed, and Blocked.
home: show the current sprint target directly in the velocity section and label all six sprint points or provide a clearly readable six-sprint axis.
home: replace outline-heavy panels with the Notion-style hierarchy of one dominant tonal scoreboard band, a restrained chart band, and divided task rows.
